::: {.why}
Every block bootstrap result depends on a number nobody defends, and picking it from the data rather than from habit is a thirty-minute job you will do once and reuse all year.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State what the block length controls, and what goes wrong at both extremes.
- Select a block length from your own data by a stated rule, and show the interval's sensitivity to that choice.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Run the sensitivity: build block-bootstrap intervals for the Sharpe ratio of one strategy at block lengths of 1, 5, 10, 20, 40 and 80 days, and plot interval width against block length. The curve flattens somewhere, and where it flattens is your answer.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Compare against a rule: the stationary bootstrap picks geometric block lengths with a mean you choose. Set that mean from the autocorrelation decay lag you measured last night, run it, and compare the interval against your flattening point. Then add `block_bootstrap_ci()` to qlib/stats.py with the block length as an explicit required argument, never a default.
:::
:::
